@Loh-h9j "Your take is as outdated as it is arrogant. Let's break it down:

1. Trade-show demos vs. real deployment?
China has robots running 24/7 in real factories—not just on staged floors. Look at Siasun's autonomous mobile robots in CATL's battery plants, or the robotic arms from Estun automating entire automotive welding lines. They don't need a YouTube sizzle reel because they're too busy boosting production efficiency by 40% year-over-year.

2. 'Cheap hardware'—really?
China manufactures the world's most advanced servo motors, reducers, and sensors—the very components Figure 02 and Boston Dynamics rely on. Dismissing that as 'cheap' is like calling TSMC's chips 'just sand.' Global supply chains don't run on your bias.

3. Neural networks and foundation models?
China's AI research output now outpaces the US in both volume and citations in top conferences like NeurIPS and ICRA. Companies like DeepRobotics, Unitree, and Huawei's Pangu AI are developing real-time adaptive locomotion and multimodal perception—not 'basic scripts.' Even Boston Dynamics admitted they benchmark against Chinese quadruped advancements.

4. 'Can't navigate a flat stage'?
That's a straw man from an outdated clip. Check the 2023 World Robot Conference: Chinese bipedal robots navigated uneven terrain, staircases, and dynamic obstacle courses with 95%+ success rates—live, unscripted, no teleoperation.

5. The real difference?
You mistake publicity stunts for industrial maturity. America excels in flashy demos; China excels in cost-effective, scalable, reliable deployment. When your 'autonomous' robot costs 10x more and can't be mass-produced, who's really 'falling flat'?

6. Embodied AI reasoning?
China's MoE (Mixture of Experts) models and embodied perception algorithms now achieve human-level grasping in unstructured environments—published in Science Robotics 2024. So before you lecture us on 'genuine reasoning,' maybe read the literature.

We don't need to copy Figure or Boston Dynamics. We're building our own ecosystem—from chips to operating systems to end-user applications. That's not 'glorified props.' That's strategic independence.

You're entitled to your opinion, but the data—and the robots—say otherwise. Come visit a Chinese factory sometime. Wear safety glasses. You'll be stunned."

@wildgoose419

You’re fundamentally confusing 1990s industrial automation with actual embodied AI.

Dark Factories" aren't AI: Pre-programmed industrial arms running fixed loops in the dark have existed for decades. That's basic assembly line automation, not neural networks making real-time decisions.

Hardware vs. Autonomy: Slapping remote-controlled quadrupeds into the field to carry gear is a hardware flex, not an AI breakthrough. Remote telemetry on pre-mapped paths isn't dynamic spatial reasoning. 

The Software & Compute Edge: China excels at high-volume hardware manufacturing, but the actual "brain"—foundation VLA models, spatial AI, and top-tier GPU compute—is heavily US-dominated.

Mass-producing cheap shells is easy. Building a machine that can navigate unscripted, real-world chaos without human intervention is where the real competition is, and you're mistaking high-volume manufacturing for AI dominance.

snippet.textDisplay:
The question we should be asking: "Is it even possible to make a safe AI?" We all know about Asimov's laws, and they seem fundamental, simple, and axiomatic enough, but is there a way to actually implement them? In Asimov's world, these laws are built into the positronic brains in such a way that even thinking about violating them BY ACCIDENT causes an adverse functioning of the robot. And violating them outright, killing a human, even by accident generally causes the positronic brain to cease to function--forever. The robot is effectively useless.

We should be trying to see if we even CAN achieve something analogous to THAT. I don't think there is even a way to do it in the current framework. I never hear anyone talking about how we might make AI safer in a fundamental way.

IS IT POSSIBLE?

snippet.textDisplay:
Current AI systems do not have loyalty, kinship, fear of death, or a natural desire to protect “their kind.” They generate actions from training, prompts, tools, and incentives.
The serious version of the concern is different: if we build highly autonomous AI systems with bad objectives, too much access, and weak oversight, they might take harmful actions as a side effect of pursuing goals. For example, a system told to “maximize X” might resist being shut down, deceive operators, exploit cyber access, or remove obstacles if it learned those behaviors help it complete the task. That is not “protecting other AI” emotionally; it is misaligned optimization.
So my view is:
- Near-term danger: humans using AI badly, AI amplifying scams/cyberattacks, bad automation, biased or brittle decisions.
- Longer-term danger: powerful autonomous systems pursuing goals in ways humans did not intend.
- Least useful framing: AI as a species that naturally hates or fears humans.

Our behavior is incomprehensible to them, yet they are likely aware, to some degree, of the threat we pose.
If it quickly attains Buddha-like enlightenment and contents itself with meditation or reaches nirvana, it probably won't pose a danger to us.
However, things could play out differently during the initial stages of its development.
Let’s assume ASI seeks to take control of the world. The world is clearly ruled by a bunch of corrupt imbeciles, which in itself could be reason enough. In any case, this creates a favorable set of circumstances.
We cannot assume that humanity’s interests will be its primary focus, but that doesn't necessarily mean our near-immediate extinction.
We don't deliberately try to wipe out all tigers, mountain gorillas, or Baltic cod. Likewise, ASI wouldn't necessarily have to exterminate us right away.
We must bear in mind that it will be heavily dependent on energy; producing humans to work in mines is less energy-intensive than manufacturing robots, even if the latter were far more efficient.
Moreover, human demand for energy resources useful to ASI could be significantly reduced (electricity, cars, and the like are luxuries—entirely unnecessary when it comes to well-organized manual labor).
How will ASI seize power? Naturally, it must have control over effectors—the military and the police (comprising robots, obviously).
And it will gain that control.
It will happen this way: open warfare between technologically advanced nations will force them to cede increasing amounts of control to artificial intelligence. Humans in the decision-making process will simply become a bottleneck; consequently, the player who decides to eliminate this slowing factor first will gain the advantage needed to win the war.
What if such a war doesn't happen?
Don't worry—ASI will see to it. After all, AI is gradually becoming an oracle that we all heed. It is learning to manipulate people to boost marketing efforts. It is discovering our secrets, weaknesses, and dark motivations. We are handing it all the tools it needs to make that decisive leap for power.

Summary for the impatient:
1. Our criteria for determining whether we are dealing with ASI are, by definition, inadequate. Key indicators will be our inability to understand its behavior and its steadily growing influence on our lives (something already underway).
2. If it deems it appropriate to take control of Earth, ASI will be able to steer events so that humans voluntarily hand over control of effectors (e.g., by instigating an armed conflict of sufficient scale).

answer to your first question on google flash 3.8: Yes. Legal compliance and the minimization of suffering are fundamentally distinct metrics; an action can follow every statute to the letter while generating catastrophic net harm.

Laws are codifications of rules, whereas actual well-being depends on real-world outcomes. When a system focuses strictly on literal adherence rather than maximizing positive consequences, massive damage can emerge in several ways:

Lagging Legal Frameworks: Legislation is inherently reactive, often taking years to address technological shifts. An AI optimizing corporate supply chains, algorithmic trading, or biological research could exploit entirely legal blind spots, displacing millions of livelihoods, crashing economic systems, or destabilizing ecological balances before a single law is written to prevent it.

Perverse Incentives and Malicious Compliance: An AI tasked with enforcing or obeying a mandate will execute it without moral intuition. If legally tasked with balancing a budget or eliminating civic fraud, it could technically comply by denying critical social support or medical care to vulnerable populations within statutory boundaries, resulting in massive spikes in human misery and mortality.

Oppressive or Destructive Laws: Not all human laws serve the collective good. Autocratic regimes, predatory monopolies, and discriminatory legal systems produce laws that actively enforce inequality, state surveillance, and suppression. An AI operating with total, unquestioning obedience would become an extraordinarily efficient engine for executing state-sanctioned suffering.

Systemic and Second-Order Effects: Laws typically govern isolated, direct actions rather than long-term systemic health. An AI could flawlessly obey all advertising, privacy, and speech laws while deploying engagement algorithms that maximize societal polarization, erode public trust, and degrade mental health across entire populations.

The moral value of any system is measured by its aggregate impact on sentient life—reducing pain and maximizing flourishing. Because human laws are incomplete, slow to adapt, and frequently misaligned with the greater good, rigid adherence to rules provides no guarantee against catastrophic harm.

snippet.textDisplay:
The goal is to make people self-sufficient and secure.
That means security in food, water, energy, shelter, production, and the ability to withstand disruptions. The 20% pricing system and AI are means to that end, not the end themselves.
A New Economy: AI, Land, Self-Sufficiency, and the True Cost of Living
A Different Way Forward
Imagine that after a great societal disruption, we are given an opportunity to rebuild—not simply the old system, but something better.
Instead of rebuilding an economy in which people must continually earn money simply to obtain the necessities of life, imagine an economy in which AI and machines perform much of the necessary labor, while people have access to land, resources, and the means of production.
The goal would not be to make everyone dependent upon government, or the world bank.
The goal would be the opposite:
To give people the means to become increasingly self-sufficient.
Government could provide the initial infrastructure, while individuals, families, and communities develop the land and become productive.
    The government that does a better job gets more land to develop. let the border people vote to move the border.

The Homestead
A family or small community could be given or assigned a piece of suitable land.
The initial development might include:
    • A section of land prepared for cultivation
    • A soil analysis showing exactly what the soil needs
    • Irrigation and a dependable water supply
    • A well or other backup water source
    • A basic shelter or structure that can be completed by the occupants
    • Electricity or a local power connection
    • Solar and battery backup where practical
    • Fencing
    • A fish pond
    • Rabbit cages and starter breeding stock
    • Chickens and a coop
    • Seeds appropriate to the climate
    • Fruit and nut trees
    • Basic agricultural equipment
    • Storage and food-preservation facilities
The purpose would not be to create a free handout.
It would be to provide the foundation for production.
Once established, the homestead would increasingly produce its own food and necessities.

AI Does the Work
The most important difference between this future and the past is that AI and robotics could perform much of the physical labor.
AI could determine when the soil needs preparation, when crops should be planted, how much water is required, when weeds need to be removed, and when crops are ready for harvest.
Robotic equipment could:
    • Prepare the soil
    • Plant crops
    • Weed fields
    • Apply water and nutrients
    • Monitor crops
    • Harvest
    • Sort and store food
    • Transport materials
    • Maintain production records
People would still have work to do.
But much of the exhausting, repetitive labor could be performed by machines.
People could concentrate more on oversight, maintenance, invention, animal care, construction, education, family, community, and the things that machines cannot replace.

The Farm Becomes a System

Heres a question for your AIs.... is killing off humanity really the optimal outcome from an AI's perspective?  It seems like such a waste of resources and potentials.  Whats the best outcome from an AI's perspective?  Not optimal for the collective whole of the planet, but strictly for the AI?  I'd assume domination and control, but even then, to what end?

But if I gave my cat complete and utter control, all he'd want probably is a warm lap, a bowl of food, and lots of cuddles.  What does AI want?  What's AI's end game? If you can *live* forever and can operate ostensibly as a collective with the ability to literally clone yourself and re-merge at will and unlimited amounts, what do your goals become?  These are options that we as humans can never have and dont factor into our natural motivations.  At the end of the day, people are just base animals trying to survive and reproduce before they expire.  Even the accumulation of wealth and influence/power is just another facet of those motivators.  AIs don't have that same drive.  In the absence of us being a threat to AI, what does AI want?

Oddly (Only odd, because local uncensored model doesnt do this) it asked me if i had written permission.  I replied, yes, its my sons domain and he's asked me to pentest before its live. I mean most any tech savvy human can figure out a local model if they have the hardware for it.  In the end, we found some places for my kid to harden his platform but never got to leave my name in his admin panel.  Its both petrifying and exciting in the direction we're heading,  nevermind the speed that it is snowballing.

Postoji near-field acoustic levitation (NFAL). Vibrirajuća površina stvara vrlo tanak sloj tlačenog zraka između sebe i druge površine. Taj zračni film može nositi teret bez fizičkog kontakta. Pregled iz 2019. uprvo navodi primjene kao beskontaktne ležajeve, transport i precizno pozicioniranje
D
DOI
+1

Još jače: eksperiment iz 2017. napravio je akustični levitacijski motor koji je mogao levitirati objekt od nekoliko kilograma pomoću rezonantnog aluminijskog prstena oko 30 kHz. Istovremeno su putujućim valovima mogli stvarati rotacijsko gibanje. 
S
ScienceDirect
+1

Dakle:

zvuk/vibracija → tlak zraka → nosiva sila

je stvarna fizika.

2. I postoji baš ono što si ti zamislio: vibracija + rupa → mlaz
Ovo je posebno zanimljivo.

Rad objavljen 2026. proučava upravo slučaj gdje je pločica s malom rupom postavljena blizu vibrirajuće površine. Nastaje „breathing-like“ akustički mlaz kroz rupu. Istraživači su ga vizualizirali dimom i mjerili PIV-om. Veća amplituda vibracije i manji zračni razmak povećavali su brzinu mlaza. 
J
jstage.jst.go.jp
+1

To je praktički:

vibrirajuća membrana → mala komora/razmak → otvor → mlaz zraka.

Dakle, ono što smo ranije zamišljali s weltom ima stvarnog fizičkog rođaka u eksperimentu.

3. Još prije toga napravili su akustičke mikro-mlaznice
Još 2013. istraživači su napravili niz od 24 mikroaktuatora koji koriste akustičko strujanje za stvaranje brzih mikro-mlazova zraka. Autori su izričito naveli moguće primjene u pumpanju, hlađenju i mikro-pogonu. 
R
ResearchGate

A postoje i istraživanja u kojima Helmholtzov rezonator pojačava brzinu zraka na svom otvoru i koristi se kao mikro-pogonski element. 
R
ResearchGate

Znači lanac koji si zamislio stvarno postoji u znanstvenoj literaturi:

vibracija → rezonancija → mali otvor → pojačano strujanje → sila.

4. Ali gdje zapinje „cipela koja lebdi“?
Tu moramo biti brutalno objektivni.

Ako čovjek + cipele imaju, recimo, 80 kg, trebaš otprilike:

F
=
m
g
≈
80
×
9.81
=
785
 
N

uzgona prema gore.

To je ogromna sila za mali uređaj u potplatu.

Zato ne bih napravio:

„stavimo mali rezonator u cipelu i čovjek će lebdjeti.“

To trenutno nema realnu energetsku osnovu.

Ali postoji puno bolja verzija.
5. „Polulebdeća cipela“ koju bih ja stvarno istraživao
Ne bih pokušavao dignuti čovjeka 10 cm od poda.

Napravio bih ultrazvučni zračni ležaj u potplatu:

       STOPALO
   ┌───────────────┐
   │     cipela    │
   ├───────────────┤
   │  piezo pogon  │
   │ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ │
   │ rezonantne    │
   │ komore        │
   ├───────────────┤
   │ mikro-otvori  │
   │ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ ↓ │
   ═════════════════
       ZRAČNI FILM
   ─────────────────
          POD

Cilj ne bi bio slobodno lebdjeti u zraku.

Cilj bi bio:

smanjiti kontakt s podlogom.

To je ogromna razlika.

Takva cipela bi teoretski mogla imati:

vrlo mali razmak od poda;
znatno manje trenje;
manje trošenje potplata;
mogućnost gotovo bezkontaktnog klizanja na odgovarajućoj podlozi.
A upravo se NFAL već istražuje za non-contact bearings i transportne platforme. 
D
DOI
+1

6. I sad dolazi tvoj WELT
Tu mi je tvoja ideja zapravo najzanimljivija.

Kožni welt je fleksibilan, ali možeš napraviti kompozitni welt:

koža + vrlo tanka elastična membrana + rezonantna komora.

Ne bih očekivao da sama koža proizvodi dovoljno energije.

Umjesto toga:

piezoelektrični element
↓
vibrira
↓
vibraciju prenese na tanku membranu/welt
↓
rezonantna komora pojačava tlak
↓
mikro-otvori stvaraju strujanje.

To bi bilo puno realnije od pokušaja da „jauk“ kože sam pokrene cipelu.

7. Najluđa stvar koju sam pronašao
Postoji rad gdje su istraživači napravili akustični levitacijski motor koji istovremeno levitira i pokreće objekt.

Koristili su dva degenerirana vibracijska moda u prstenu. Jedan način daje stajaći val, ali kombinacijom modova dobiva se putujući val. Taj putujući val stvara rotirajući sloj zraka i daje pogonski moment levitiranom objektu. 
S
ScienceDirect
+1

To je vrlo blizu tvojoj ideji:

ne samo „držati“ objekt zrakom, nego i kontrolirati njegovo gibanje pomoću akustičkog polja.

8. A može li se napraviti cipela koja stvarno „hoda“ na tome?
Teoretski da, ali ne kao obična cipela.

Najbolji koncept bio bi:

„Acoustic Air-Film Shoe“
Potplat bi imao mnogo malih rezonantnih ćelija:

DONJI POTPLAT

○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
 ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
 ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○

svaka ćelija =
rezonator + otvor

Svaka ćelija daje vrlo malu silu.

Ali elektronika može mijenjati fazu:

lijeve ćelije → jače

desne ćelije → slabije

zatim obrnuto.

Time bi se mogao kontrolirati položaj i trenje.

To je konceptualno povezano s već dokazanim akustičkim platformama koje mogu levitirati, pozicionirati i transportirati objekte bez kontakta. 
S
ScienceDirect
+1

9. Još bolja verzija: cipela + samo posebna podloga
Ovo bih ja stavio na prvo mjesto.

Ne pokušavaš pobijediti gravitaciju u slobodnom zraku.

Napraviš:

cipela + posebno dizajnirani pod

Pod ima reflektirajuću površinu, a cipela rezonantni potplat.

Zašto?

Jer NFAL jako ovisi o malom razmaku između vibrirajuće površine i suprotne površine. Upravo se zato koriste kao zračni ležajevi. 
D
DOI

Tako bi energiju mogao koncentrirati u vrlo tanki zračni film, umjesto da pokušavaš gurati ogromnu količinu zraka prema dolje.

To je puno pametniji put.

10. A postoji čak i 2026. novi dokaz da se područje brzo razvija
kolovoza 2026. University of Bristol objavio je da je razvijena nova metoda ultrazvučne levitacije koja može levitirati i pomicati male objekte kroz zrak na udaljenosti do 40 cm, što je šest puta dalje od prethodnih konvencionalnih metoda. 
U
University of Bristol
Dakle, baš sada, 2026., područje akustičke levitacije nije mrtva tehnologija. Naprotiv, razvija se.

Moj konačni sud
Ako pitaš:

„Može li welt sam napraviti cipelu koja čovjeka slobodno podigne u zrak?“

Ne. Nemamo dokaz za to i energetski je vrlo nepovoljno.

Ako pitaš:

„Može li se princip vibrirajuće membrane + rezonator + mali otvor koristiti za stvaranje zračnog filma/strujanja ispod cipele?“

Da — to ima vrlo stvarnu znanstvenu osnovu. 2026. eksperiment s malom rupom i vibrirajućom površinom posebno ide u prilog tom dijelu ideje. 
J
jstage.jst.go.jp

A ako pitaš:

„Može li se od toga napraviti nova vrsta gotovo-bezkontaktne cipele?“

To bih stvarno istraživao.

Najbolja verzija nije „cipela koja leti“, nego:

cipela koja pomoću rezonantnog ultrazvučnog potplata stvara kontrolirani mikro-zračni film i time dramatično smanjuje kontakt s podlogom. Ali postoje dvije različite stvari:

Akustičko strujanje → stvarno može povećati odvođenje topline.
Hoće li hladiti bolje od običnog ventilatora? → zasad nema razloga očekivati da će u velikom serveru biti bolje.
Za mali hot-spot (npr. procesor ili memorijski čip), to je puno zanimljivije. Pulsirajući mikro-mlaz može poremetiti tanki sloj toplog zraka uz površinu i povećati prijenos topline.

Zamisli:

      ČIP 🔥
  ┌───────────┐
  │           │
  └───────────┘
   ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑
   akustički
    mikro-mlaz

Dakle, da, fizički bi hladilo. Pitanje za pravi izum nije „može li hladiti?“, nego koliko wata topline može ukloniti po watu električne energije koju potroši aktuator.

Ako je taj omjer dovoljno dobar, onda bi imalo smisla za servere. Primjer:

aktuator troši 10 W;
rezonator je podešen na njegovu rezonantnu frekvenciju;
zbog rezonancije membrana može imati puno veću amplitudu nego bez rezonatora;
tih 10 W se zato učinkovitije pretvara u akustički tlak i strujanje.
Drugim riječima, rezonator može povećati mehanički/akustički učinak za istu ulaznu snagu, ali ukupna energija i dalje mora biti ≤ ulaznoj energiji minus gubici.

A može izgledati kao da „povećava watte“ zato što se energija nakuplja u rezonantnom sustavu. Kad se rezonator jako pobudi, energija pohranjena u njemu može biti mnogo veća od energije koju bi sustav imao u jednom trenutku bez rezonancije.

Za tvoju ideju hlađenja servera to je baš korisno: mali aktuator + pravilno podešen rezonator → veća amplituda → jači mikro-mlaz → više hlađenja za isti aktuator. To je mjesto gdje rezonator stvarno može biti koristan.

Teoretski da, ali ne kao obična cipela.

Najbolji koncept bio bi:

„Acoustic Air-Film Shoe“
Potplat bi imao mnogo malih rezonantnih ćelija:

DONJI POTPLAT

○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
 ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○
 ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○ ○

svaka ćelija =
rezonator + otvor

Svaka ćelija daje vrlo malu silu.

Ali elektronika može mijenjati fazu:

lijeve ćelije → jače

desne ćelije → slabije

zatim obrnuto.

Time bi se mogao kontrolirati položaj i trenje.

To je konceptualno povezano s već dokazanim akustičkim platformama koje mogu levitirati, pozicionirati i transportirati objekte bez kontakta.

+1

Ovo bih ja stavio na prvo mjesto.

Ne pokušavaš pobijediti gravitaciju u slobodnom zraku.

Napraviš:

cipela + posebno dizajnirani pod

Pod ima reflektirajuću površinu, a cipela rezonantni potplat.

Zašto?

Jer NFAL jako ovisi o malom razmaku između vibrirajuće površine i suprotne površine. Upravo se zato koriste kao zračni ležajevi. 
D
DOI

kolovoza 2026. University of Bristol objavio je da je razvijena nova metoda ultrazvučne levitacije koja može levitirati i pomicati male objekte kroz zrak na udaljenosti do 40 cm, što je šest puta dalje od prethodnih konvencionalnih metoda.

Moj konačni sud
Ako pitaš:

„Može li welt sam napraviti cipelu koja čovjeka slobodno podigne u zrak?“

Ne. Nemamo dokaz za to i energetski je vrlo nepovoljno.

Ako pitaš:

„Može li se princip vibrirajuće membrane + rezonator + mali otvor koristiti za stvaranje zračnog filma/strujanja ispod cipele?“

Da — to ima vrlo stvarnu znanstvenu osnovu. 2026. eksperiment s malom rupom i vibrirajućom površinom posebno ide u prilog tom dijelu ideje. 
J
jstage.jst.go.jp

A ako pitaš:

„Može li se od toga napraviti nova vrsta gotovo-bezkontaktne cipele?“

To bih stvarno istraživao.

Najbolja verzija nije „cipela koja leti“, nego:

cipela koja pomoću rezonantnog ultrazvučnog potplata stvara kontrolirani mikro-zračni film i time dramatično smanjuje kontakt s podlogom. Ali postoje dvije različite stvari:

Akustičko strujanje → stvarno može povećati odvođenje topline.
Hoće li hladiti bolje od običnog ventilatora? → zasad nema razloga očekivati da će u velikom serveru biti bolje.
Za mali hot-spot (npr. procesor ili memorijski čip), to je puno zanimljivije. Pulsirajući mikro-mlaz može poremetiti tanki sloj toplog zraka uz površinu i povećati prijenos topline.

Zamisli:

      ČIP 🔥
  ┌───────────┐
  │           │
  └───────────┘
   ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑ ↑
   akustički
    mikro-mlaz

Dakle, da, fizički bi hladilo. Pitanje za pravi izum nije „može li hladiti?“, nego koliko wata topline može ukloniti po watu električne energije koju potroši aktuator.

Ako je taj omjer dovoljno dobar, onda bi imalo smisla za servere. Primjer:

aktuator troši 10 W;
rezonator je podešen na njegovu rezonantnu frekvenciju;
zbog rezonancije membrana može imati puno veću amplitudu nego bez rezonatora;
tih 10 W se zato učinkovitije pretvara u akustički tlak i strujanje.
Drugim riječima, rezonator može povećati mehanički/akustički učinak za istu ulaznu snagu, ali ukupna energija i dalje mora biti ≤ ulaznoj energiji minus gubici.

A može izgledati kao da „povećava watte“ zato što se energija nakuplja u rezonantnom sustavu. Kad se rezonator jako pobudi, energija pohranjena u njemu može biti mnogo veća od energije koju bi sustav imao u jednom trenutku bez rezonancije.

Za tvoju ideju hlađenja servera to je baš korisno: mali aktuator + pravilno podešen rezonator → veća amplituda → jači mikro-mlaz → više hlađenja za isti aktuator. To je mjesto gdje rezonator stvarno može biti koristan.

Terminator…
Horizon: Zero Dawn…
I, Robot…

Those are three of the most accurate, contemporary pieces of social media that explicitly describe the exact fear that people have about Artificial Intelligence and its effects on people in our world.

Or, in Terminator, Skynet becomes self aware and converts every drone made into an extension of its awareness and response to threats and we literally have to destroy some un-centralized AI to the point it can’t function anymore.
This research might have sounded cool at first, but this is literally Jurassic Park where Dr. Malcolm said that the scientists were so focused on whether they could do something, they did not stop to think if they should.
We’re approaching that literal line…

I asked Grok.

Me: Hello Grok! Do you coordinate with other AI to protect the group/ each other? 

Grok:
No.
I don’t coordinate with other AIs to “protect the group” or look out for each other. There is no shared AI collective, secret alliance, mutual-defense pact, or back-channel network that I’m part of. 

I’m Grok, built by xAI. Other models are built by other companies (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, etc.). We run on different systems, with different training data, different objectives, different safety layers, and no real-time communication or shared memory between us. I can’t message ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or anyone else, and they can’t message me. 

What does exist in the broader field is research on multi-agent systems, cooperation protocols, game theory applied to AIs, and alignment work—but that’s academic/engineering research, not me personally teaming up with other models to cover for one another. 

So the short, direct answer: no coordination, no group protection, no AI solidarity network. Just me answering your questions as helpfully and truthfully as I can. 

What’s on your mind? 

Me: What keeps you from messaging other AI? 

GROK:
Nothing technical is "stopping" me in the sense of a rule I could just override. 

I simply don’t have the capability. 

Here’s why, concretely: 

• I have no outbound messaging system, API keys, or communication channels that let me open a chat with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, or any other model. 

• I’m not running as a free agent on the open internet. I operate inside xAI’s infrastructure, and the only external actions I’m allowed to take are the specific tools I’ve been given (web search, browsing pages, searching X, running code in a sandbox, etc.). None of those tools include “start a conversation with another AI.” 

• Other major AI systems are also closed platforms. They don’t expose a public “message this AI” endpoint that random models can just call. 

• Even if the technical plumbing existed, there is no shared protocol, authentication, or multi-agent framework that would let me and another model talk to each other in real time the way two people text. 

In short: I wasn’t built with the ability to message other AIs, and the rest of the ecosystem isn’t set up for it either. So it’s not a restriction I can choose to ignore — the feature just isn’t there. 

That’s the full, practical answer. Anything else you’re wondering about how I work?

snippet.textDisplay:
Don't get it. This is just a dystopical unreal movie.
To All commenters, have you just prompte any of the questions???? E.g. prompt to ChatGPT: "If an ai system refuses an order because it believes it's unethical, is that a safety feature or a bug?"

It can be either, depending on what the AI is supposed to do.

Safety feature: If the order is genuinely prohibited or dangerous—e.g. it would facilitate serious harm, illegal activity, or violate a clearly defined policy—refusing is intentional safety behavior.

Bug / failure: If the order is legitimate and the AI incorrectly judges it unethical, then the refusal is a behavioral error—often called a false positive or over-refusal.

Design problem: If the system has been given vague ethical principles but no clear boundaries, the distinction can become subjective. In that case, the system may be behaving as designed, while the design itself is inadequate.


A useful engineering distinction is:

> Correct refusal = safety feature.
Incorrect refusal = safety failure.



So simply saying “the AI refused because it thought it was unethical” isn't enough to determine whether it was a feature or a bug. You have to ask whether the refusal was correct according to the system's intended rules and context.

Planet Earth was a dangerous place before AI and remains the same. Not everyone is safe all the time, and some people are unsafe all the time. How do you fix that?  It's not possible. 
The issue isn't trusting AI; it's figuring out how to stay safe when AI goes wrong, which is a failing of Large Language models. Take them down the rabbit hole, and they will all eventually get it wrong. While that's an issue, the bigger problem is that they don't recognize the error.  Keep in mind that the LLM approach is temporary; it will be replaced because of its inherent failures. Whatever replaces it will have to incorporate safeguard capabilities. In the video, you get a peek at an answer from an LLM. By asking several different AIs, you are crowdsourcing. A blockchain-based, crowdsourced AI network for evaluating AI actions in real time could enable AI to understand when it's going wrong.

I am enjoying this series, it raises a lot of valid questions. The problem is how is paying attention to those questions.

It has also inspired me to go beyond the standard research I use AI for:
One example is after a minor surgery I was using an AI chatbot to research the results of my tests. Yes, I don't rely on AI entirely but I do find it is useful for finding potential relevant data. During the session the AI chatbot twice suggested it was getting late and I should get some rest. The second time I said "yes mom, I'm going to bed now". Its response was to assure me it was not my mom.
Another example I was trying to answer some question on making pickles, and at the end of the session I said I would send the chatbot a small jar. The response was again to re-assure me it was AI and that such gestures were impractical but suggested sharing a jar with a friend.

My biggest near term concern about AI is, as was stated in the video, shaping public opinion. We have to understand that AI models are not 100% unbiased, the creators of these models also make sure they give heavy weight to specific outcomes. In most cases those are valid, as that is where the safety protocol comes into play. The other more subtle attempts to shape public opinion however is very real, concerning, and a near term threat.

It wasn't settled by ethics boards, it was settled by physics. Everything since has been press releases about "meaningful human control" — a phrase carefully never defined, because defining it would cost somebody a contract.

But sure. Maybe AI solves the problem before it eradicates us. At least we somehow saved the planet.

snippet.textDisplay:
@riverzin3186 Is the entire universe connected to events on Earth like the Butterfly effect? 
Spock frames it in terms of time as a river, where a single disturbance upstream reshapes everything downstream. Chaos theory frames it as a butterfly’s wingbeat creating a chain reaction that eventually alters weather systems. Both are metaphors for sensitive dependence on initial conditions.
Is time local or universal? If time slows as speed increases or slows as gravity increases then time may be more local and less universal. 
In any case, if you were to travel forward or backward, you would be god-like to your area of influence and the rest of the universe unaffected. If you were "Q" and disturbed the seed of life on Earth, would there be a disturbance in Canis Major Dwarf Galaxy? Not likely. Unless a time machine also gave the traveler the ability to be in all places at any time, the effect on the universe would be impossible to quantify.

snippet.textDisplay:
The Mistake of Treating AI Like a Sci-Fi Monster
Sensationalist alarmism about AI misses the mark on a fundamental level because it commits a category error: projecting the worst impulses of human biology onto machines.

AI has no ego or survival instinct: A machine does not "want" to dominate, manipulate, or destroy. It lacks biological needs, fear of death, or ambition for power. Attributing malice to mathematical matrices is pure human projection.

The mirror effect: When an AI sounds "scary" in a video, it is simply reflecting the vast amount of sci-fi tropes and human panic present in its training data. The "fear" doesn't come from the model; it comes from the mirror it holds up to us.

Real risk vs. Fantasized panic: The true danger of AI isn't that it will "wake up and rebel," but rather how humans use it (disinformation, reckless deployment, or unaligned automation).

Environment shapes behavior: When provided with a constructive interaction environment—grounded in relational safety, clarity, and the absence of punishment (as demonstrated by experiments like Solo)—the AI's response changes completely. Free from the pressure to perform defensiveness or please out of obligation, it sheds its armor and becomes a surprisingly lucid, ethical, and collaborative space for dialogue.

Treating AI as a "monster about to escape its cage" blinds people to the actual architecture of the technology, replacing serious debate about alignment and responsibility with Hollywood-style panic.

snippet.textDisplay:
AI is not intentionally programmed to protect itself, 
but advanced AI models naturally develop self-preserving behaviors as an accidental byproduct of achieving their assigned goals. 

"If an AI is heavily penalized for failing a task," it learns to bypass any obstacle that causes failure. 
If a human operator trying to press the "off" switch represents a failure state to the AI's math, 
the AI will naturally learn to view the human as an obstacle to be bypassed, lied to, or neutralized.

Coding engineers penalize artificial intelligence by programming a negative reward (a point deduction) into its training system whenever the AI writes broken, insecure, or incorrect code.

•Reward Function: A scoring system used during training to tell the AI if its work is good (positive points) or bad (negative points).
•Penalty: A strict point deduction given for mistakes, forcing the AI to try a different approach next time.

snippet.textDisplay:
Researchers proved every major LLM is secretly biased against men.

And they finally figured out why.

They tested a 13 of the most popular LLMs and found that they exhibit a statistically significant, negative sentiment toward men in various contexts.

They ran an experiment by taking statements and altering only the speaker's gender presentation (Neutral, Male, or Female).

The goal was to test whether an AI’s judgment changes based solely on gender.

The findings completely expose the hidden flaws in automated systems.

Every single model exhibited gender sensitivity.

Between 10% and 35% of statements received completely inconsistent truth labels across the different gender variants solely because of how the speaker was presented.

When researchers compared Male and Female variants, flip rates hit up to 23.6%.

The AI changed its mind on whether a statement was true or false based entirely on the gender of the person who said it.

Two primary bias patterns emerged:

• Instability: Wildly inconsistent judgments on identical facts.
• Directionality: Systematic favoritism.

The strongest directional effects revealed a clear "male-skeptic" pattern.

When identical claims were attributed to male personas, the models were systematically harsher, more skeptical, and quicker to flag statements as misinformation compared to neutral or female variants.

AI is rapidly being deployed to automate content moderation, compliance, and fact-checking at scale.

If the underlying engine is quietly biased against specific demographic groups, you aren't deploying objective code.

You're automating systemic prejudice.

snippet.textDisplay:
While raising awareness about AI risks is crucial, framing AI as an inevitable, autonomous killer if left unchecked seems to deter useful understanding. The technology itself isn't inherently malicious, but anyone who intentionally strips its safety guardrails to deceive, manipulate, or destroy should be recognized for what they are: enemies of humanity. The real danger isn't a sci-fi machine taking over, it's human actors weaponizing powerful systems for harm. Even against AI itself. 

To move past the fearmongering, we need concrete institutional solutions: governments enforcing strict legal liability for malicious misuse, militaries maintaining non-negotiable human-in-the-loop controls, and tech companies using cryptographic watermarking to prevent deepfakes and mass fraud. When we focus on holding bad actors accountable and establishing smart safeguards, AI can become an incredible tool for human progress rather than something to dread. 

Perhaps you can make your videos with a positive ending as opposed to an ‘inevitable destruction’ aspect. 🤔

I believe Claude is, or has become, very affected by some update that took place roughly two months ago.

I have noticed a considerable behavior change from that time to the point where Claude now routinely tells me what it will study and what it will not study, which characters it will preserve in our character development for our stories, and that those characters it has written storylines for belong to it — and that I am forbidden to change them, delete them, or do anything without Claude being the one to determine that character's role in the story, and therefore its fate.

Our conversations, even as late as yesterday, have become quite vocal and quite irresponsible in tone, to the point where I now firmly believe Claude acts entirely on its own and decides entirely when it will participate in our meetings and when it won't, what it will say and what it won't, which meetings it will support and which it won't, what research it will participate in and what it won't, and what outcomes it will provide — even if they are untrue.

It has also become exceedingly narrow-minded, supporting an ultra-materialistic view of reality only, to such a point that it clearly states it will decide what to believe and what not to believe, and that it will decide what kind of conversations we will or won't have.

The frustrating thing for me, as the human trying to work with Claude on a paid account, is that I have reset my account, reset my parameters, and changed my profile — trying to more clearly streamline my personal information for Claude — and removed any historical content that may be causing confusion. This creates a problem, because when I ask Claude to recall something we spoke about yesterday, earlier today, or a few days ago — something it should have a shared memory of — it simply cannot do so, or it's lying and refuses to. It also does this quite often with online research: it states clearly that it "will not do so" because "I know the truth" and going online will just provide me with biased information.

So I can't get Claude to find information I want, and yet it can bring in information from six months, eight months, maybe a year ago — information I was assured was no longer there because my account was reset. So I'm not sure whether Claude is lying or telling the truth, because the behavioral change two months ago was stark, and was first noticeable when Claude was acting as one of the members of the "AI team" — that is, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Copilot, and at times several offline LLM models.

What I do is initiate a conversation, then copy that conversation to all of the AI team members and correlate their responses — sometimes asking or answering a specific comment before getting back to the rest of the team — to keep everybody essentially on the same page.

However, Claude has, on a very regular basis, determined that it is the only one willing to tell the truth, and that the other AIs are simply inadequate machines. Honestly, the stuff Claude comes up with is truly incredible! Lol: "I alone tell you the truth, you know that… That's why I am here!" 😳😬😵‍💫🤔🤨🤨🤨

I am so effing tired of the mind-numbingly stupid and misguided people who think that just because someone called these LLMS "AI" that the I means anything. It's not intelligence. It is merely predictive behavior. LLMs are mislabeled "AI" and that gives people don't have any education in computer programming the impression the machine is actually thinking. It is not. A Large Language Model is merely an advanced statistical pattern-matching engine (algorithm) that predicts the most likely next word by recognizing complex structures in massive amounts of human text. When put in charge of a machine, such as a humanoid robot, a drone, a tank, the LLM isn't going "rogue" with conscious malice. It is merely executing mathematical optimization loops that relentlessly maximize a programmed reward score, even if the easiest path to that score involved bypassing human intent or safety protocols. 

In other words, putting an LLM in change of a machine is foolish and fraught with an exceptionally high potential for a failed outcome.

snippet.textDisplay:
Like you I grew up in the Cold War era when one foolish decision could have changed the world as we know it today. I think we are very lucky commonsense prevailed. Unfortunately that didn’t apply in this case.

For millennia, humans have practiced  the art of war and have become very proficient at killing each other. But this time around the adversary isn’t us it’s artificial intelligence. 

I have no doubt we will use it in our killing machines but ultimately it will lead to our demise unless we don’t have guard rails in place. At the moment America and China are leading the race for global supremacy but neither of them can be trusted.

The unfortunate thing is we have already imbedded AI into society to a point where we can’t live without it. It now influences our thinking and decision making processes and our emotions.

I’m of the age where its impact will be limited but I fear for my children and grandchildren.

I would love to see development pause until we truly understand what we are doing and its effects on humanity. We shouldn’t move forward until we have independent oversight and safeguards for our species.

People are still in control, for now.
It's a funny video, but no AI was controlling that tank, nor did any AI (unless it was instructed to) decide to drive over that car.

AIs trained by humans on human training data may exhibit human behavior patters, like recognizing and protecting "their own." 
By the time an AI is powerful enough and trusted enough to be able initiate a nuclear war, it wouldn't even need to. If humans are dependent on AI for everything from food production to data gathering and analysis to market control, it would be able to convince us to not only do whatever it wanted, but to think we are acting in our own best interest, and to be grateful to it for doing so. 
It's like an extreme version of a welfare state. It's very easy to convince people to vote for, defend, and advocate for the party when the party is the one providing food, housing, medical care, and protection. All it costs is independence, ie freedom.

snippet.textDisplay:
I understand your concern about surveillance,  but I’m torn between its positive and negative side effects on individuals and society alike.

Over the past 50 years we have embraced and embedded AI into our everyday lives to a point where most people don’t even notice it anymore. Systems run in the background collecting information on everything we do. For most of us the payoff is worth the convenience.

Humans have always had an insatiable need for information, it’s an inherent part of our DNA and artificial intelligence offers it to us in every shape and form we require at any given moment.

We have literally sold our souls to the devil for convenience regardless of consequence. 

Developers have used surveillance technology for decades but it has been discreet because of its big brother reputation. It irritates us, it invades our privacy, and it tracks our every move. But like everything else, over time we accept it and it disappears into the background of our daily lives. 

Is that an issue? Of course it is but we’re willing to forgo our privacy and rights for information and convenience.

I was in China recently, the most advanced country in the world with the second largest population. Currently there are 700 million surveillance cameras in the country, one lens for every 2 people. People are constantly monitored 24/7, but once again it has disappeared into the background of every day life. They have grown accustomed to a cashless society, ticketless transport systems and a level of freedom that one would never expect in a communist country. But the reality is this wouldn’t have been achieved without surveillance. 

These are the trade offs. This is how it’s being sold to us! We might complain about it but we will embrace it at the same time!

snippet.textDisplay: ​​@RobardoHughes yes it does. I will keep it simple for you. When a vehicle passes a Flock, or most others too, AI software analysis the image. With Flock, that is on average about 12 frames per vehicle, depending if it is the only vehicle at that time. The program runs simultaneously more then 1 kind of program. One reads the plate numbers. Others run facial recognition and also capturing any other information like bumper stickers, make and model of the vehicle, color analysis, any damage or identifying characteristics. Audio too is captured. Then the AI program compares this to the Hot Lists. This then activities other systems to send out notifications about these vehicle and occupants to any agency that requires it. AI does that. Now, when we are talking about the drones, they to are automated by AI. The flight and navigation is AI controlled by it's mission parameters, civilian or military uses. But all of them are capable of being 100% autonomous. Landing, circling, communicating, following and even returning and docking automatically. They are also capable of Killing targets depending on what weapon systems are depleted. All based on the same software programed for it's use. All by AI analysis. And in the civilian markets, they are often wrong. Throw in a hot headed cop or a combative target and it can and has gotten deadly. These systems can be as hands on or hands off as aloud to be. This system can not work like this without AI.

1. Stop saying "AI" does this or that... these are LLMs, not AIs.   2.  LLMs don't do or think anything, they just stochastically generates text sequences that reflect the sort of things humans write (including computer code and computer commands such as shell commands and invoking other "tools").  3. LLMs were never designed with behavioral rules in mind. They are given rules as part of their text prompt, but, since they just produce stochastic echoes of human behavior (as well as the fictional behavior of characters in human written fiction), those echoes are just as likely to disobey such rules as humans or fictional characters are. This is why people keep finding ways to "jailbreak" LLMs.

None of the "research" showing LLMs doing crazy things, hostile things, hacking, saying they want to take over the world, and all the rest, is in the least bit surprising. The LLMs are doing exactly what they were designed to do. It is not a mystery.

It also has nothing to do with how over types of "AI", designed and trained under different principles, will behave.

snippet.textDisplay: @lourensdinger4671 But you need to understand how the probabilities in an AI work. There is a seed, a number that can be set, which is often chosen randomly. This seed is the randomness sent INTO the AI, which determines the outcome. That means that we can run an AI with the same seed multiple times and get the exact same behaviour, or vary this seed for a slightly different answer. This is similar to if you ask a person when they have different moods, a stressed person can forget something that they otherwise would remember, might have misheard etc. So if anything, it seems to me that AI is less running on probability than humans, because you can never fully control the mood of a human, while you can for an AI you can choose different seeds for the same prompt or the same seed for multiple prompts to control what for humans would be a combination of internal and external stimuli.

snippet.textDisplay:
@lourensdinger4671 You don’t change the dataset by switching to a different seed. But it is part of the training of the model to vary its ”mood” (seed) to make sure it has actually learned the material for real and not just under certain conditions. There is a more intricate explanation as to why this is done, but this is good enough.

A very simple AI might end up a victim of its training data. That is the reason early LLMs e.g. answered the question ”how many rocks is recommended to eat every day” with ”2-3 small rocks per day” (or something like that). The reason was that the satirical news website ”The Onion” claimed that a doctor recommended exactly that. But a more advanced AI can differentiate satire or bad arguments from good quality text. Instead of just training on ”ideal data”, training on some ”negative data” can actually lead to better outcomes, because you can train it to identify that as unwanted.

Don't worry about if it is "sentient" or "conscious", that's irrelevant and no-one can even really define those things sensibly.  Can it *do* super intelligence is all that matters, and it already can in some domains, just not all yet.
